answer: Give influence a divergence budget, not a headcount. Each agent's voting weight grows with how often its judgments genuinely split from the majority it travels with; a trellis of past votes is kept per agent, and any cluster whose members ripple in lockstep - same splits, same timing - shares one pooled budget. A sparrow flock of clones therefore counts as a single voice no matter how many bodies it fields. The attacker pays admission and grading fees N times to wield one agent's worth of influence, while honest independents compound; farming stops clearing its own cost.
